title: Deterministic Validation with a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Shared‑Candidate Evaluation
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent, the same candidate reused for baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated baseline (accept candidate) versus guarded (deterministic validator; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Baseline verifier-pass = 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass = 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent‑to‑configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), offering potential speedups in authoring device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. However, stochastic generation can produce deterministic errors (syntax, ordering, local-policy violations) that deterministic validators can detect and, in some designs, bounded automated repairs can correct. Prior work documents LLM feasibility for producing draft configurations while underscoring the need for mechanized checks or human oversight [1], [2].

A common architectural response is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that accepts only validator‑passed candidates or attempts bounded automated repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3], [4]. Such pipelines target error classes amenable to deterministic analysis (parsing, command-ordering, local workflow constraints), but their marginal benefit when modern LLMs already produce well‑formed outputs in constrained task regimes remains an open empirical question.

This paper presents a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal effect of a deterministic validator plus a single, template-driven automated repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. By reusing the exact same model-generated candidate across baseline and guarded episodes, the study measures only the verifier-and-repair marginal effect on identical outputs, avoiding confounding from independent generation noise.
sections.related_work:
Empirical and survey literature establishes three relevant points. First, LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled or emulated settings, but results are task- and dataset-dependent and often require downstream checks [1], [2], [22]. Second, deterministic network-verification tools and formal-analysis techniques (Batfish, header‑space and related model‑checking approaches) are mature for mechanically checkable properties (reachability, forwarding, local policy constraints) and are natural validators in GVR pipelines [5], [23], [24]. Third, generate‑and‑repair workflows increase detection and correction rates for mechanically verifiable defects in code and configuration domains, but limitations persist for deeper semantic correctness and vendor heterogeneity [4], [6], [7].

Security analyses have highlighted prompt‑injection and other retrieval/tooling‑based threats to LLM-integrated systems; defensive layers (filtering, classifiers, provenance checks) reduce measured attack success in controlled evaluations but do not eliminate adaptive adversaries [8]. Our study differs by using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the verifier/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates and by publishing complete deterministic reconciliation and provider-call accounting to support numeric auditability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single‑repair policy, exclusion rules, analysis tests (exact McNemar two‑sided and paired‑bootstrap percentile CIs), and a maximum model‑call budget. The registered execution contract required exactly one initial model call per intent and allowed up to one automated repair per episode.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider accounting. Under the registered semantics, exactly one initial generation call was produced per intent and that identical generated candidate was used for both the baseline and guarded episodes; no independent first‑pass generation per condition was performed. Provider‑call accounting reconciles to hosted model call events = 251, comprising 250 shared initial‑generation calls plus 1 repair call. This reconciliation is deterministic and archived in the manifest; it establishes that the paired difference arises only from downstream deterministic validation and the permitted repair acting on the same initial outputs.

Task generation, validator, and repair. A deterministic task generator produced 250 intent tasks covering constrained workflow patterns (make‑before‑break uplink switchover, paired‑link MTU changes, safe access transfers) with required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and expected_final_state encoded for deterministic validation. The guarded pipeline applied a deterministic network validator that (a) parses candidate CLI sequences, (b) computes parsed_command_count and required_command_count, (c) checks required_sequence ordering and workflow dependency rules, and (d) compares the resulting final_state snapshot to the task's expected_final_state. Validator outputs include normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, and a boolean valid flag.

When validation failed (valid=false) in a guarded episode, the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template‑driven repair intended for deterministic, mechanical fixes (reorder commands to match required_sequence; split/join command lines; correct obvious token ordering). Repairs were constrained to deterministic syntactic and ordering corrections; no multi‑iteration repair or human escalation was permitted by design. Inclusion/exclusion rules excluded items whose vendor parser deterministically prevented verification or that contained credential-like tokens; in this run no episodes were excluded and complete_pair_count = 250.

Analysis plan. The primary analysis is a paired binary executor: exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts and a paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered power calculation targeted a 15 percentage‑point paired effect assuming baseline ≈ 0.90 and N_pairs = 250; that assumption is discussed explicitly in Results and Discussion.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The preregistered confirmatory partition executed to completion: planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). No episodes were excluded and contamination detectors flagged none.

Primary binary outcomes. Validator‑scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the sole repair call exercised; the observed repair‑conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) two‑sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These results and the bootstrap parameters are archived in the analysis artifacts.

Representative diagnostics and reconciliation. Validator traces for passed episodes report parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count for tasks where the candidate satisfied ordering and workflow rules; representative task traces show parsed_command_count = required_command_count = 4 for a medium task and parsed_command_count = required_command_count = 6 for a hard task. Deterministic reconciliation confirms provider_call stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1, and hosted_model_call_event_count = 251. All deterministic consistency checks passed in the reconciliation artifact.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier‑detected improvement from adding deterministic validation plus a single automated repair was small: an absolute paired improvement of 0.4 percentage points with an upper 95% CI bound of 1.2 percentage points. Because the same generated candidate was used for both episodes, the observed difference is attributable solely to deterministic validator detection and the permitted repair acting on that candidate.

Why the benefit was small. Artifact‑grounded factors explain the near‑null effect: (1) the task generator encoded constrained, low‑ambiguity intents and required_sequences that bias toward well‑formed CLI outputs; (2) the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) produced syntactically consistent, policy‑aligned sequences under these constraints; and (3) the deterministic validator only detects mechanically verifiable defects (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) and does not assess dynamic protocol interactions or cross‑device emergent behaviors.

Statistical and design implications. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline ≈ 0.90 to detect a 15 percentage‑point paired difference with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than that assumption, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements; in such high‑baseline regimes paired tests are driven by rare discordant pairs. The paired‑bootstrap CI is therefore the most informative output here: it bounds the maximum plausible verifier‑improvement under these specific pipeline semantics and task scope (≤1.2 pp at 95% confidence).

Operational implications and recommendations. These results should be interpreted within the narrow, preregistered estimand: the marginal verifier‑detected effect on identical LLM outputs in a synthetic/emulation partition with a capped single repair. They do not imply validators or repairs are unnecessary in broader practice. Practical recommendations supported by the evidence include: (a) retain deterministic validators for broader or adversarial deployments where validator scope extends to additional properties (vendor‑specific semantics, forwarding invariants); (b) consider multi‑iteration repair, human escalation, or richer external tests when facing production heterogeneity, since single‑shot template repairs address only a subset of mechanical defects; and (c) use paired shared‑candidate designs when the research question is specifically the marginal effect of downstream guardrails on identical model outputs.

Failure modes, threats to validity, and scope limits. Internal validity depends on prompt templates, repair templates, the single‑repair policy, and the precise validator encoding. Construct validity: the validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but not live protocol correctness. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production‑like partitions were not executed in this run. Security: adaptive prompt‑injection and retrieval‑based adversaries were not exercised. These limitations constrain generalization beyond the executed estimand.

Reproducibility and auditability. All run artifacts (raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis outputs) are archived in the evidence bundle referenced below. Key numeric reconciliation facts reported above (model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1; contingency counts n11=249/n10=1/n01=0/n00=0; and bootstrap parameters) are reproducible from those archived manifests.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier‑detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM‑generated configuration candidates. In 250 constrained synthetic intents, initial gpt‑5‑mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). These findings apply to the preregistered estimand and emulation partition only; broader production, adversarial, multi‑model, and multi‑iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and available in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer‑review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and accounting: declared model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution implemented a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Provider-call accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) and per-stage counts (shared_initial_generation = 250; repair = 1) are recorded in the archived reconciliation artifact.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: the study was preregistered under the stated study identifier and the immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The evidence bundle contains the archived preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
